requirements.statement: Use stable, resolvable identifiers so metadata records and their relationships remain reliably identifiable across catalogues.
Represent catalogue relationships as machine-interpretable links that support a health-data knowledge graph.
Define review responsibilities for metadata received by harvesting or direct publishing.
Make metadata sufficiently interpretable and informative to support machine-assisted search, including semantic and generative-AI use.
Allow dataset discovery to be refined using health categories, access bodies, holder types, personal-data categories, age ranges, population size, quality labels and coding information.
Adapt displayed filters to whether the catalogue query concerns personal or non-personal data.
Use semantic annotations and shared coding vocabularies to make health descriptions interoperable and searchable.
Describe at least one safe sample distribution for non-public datasets so users can prepare analyses without accessing sensitive records.
Accompany sample data with definitions of its variables in a data dictionary.
Allow applicants to identify the variables they need, supporting data minimisation.
Provide usable descriptions of data structures and coding so datasets can be understood and processed consistently.
Describe logical dataset subdivisions and their relationships where large holdings need to be partitioned.
State intellectual-property and reuse conditions, including those on sample distributions.
Link to descriptive analytics that help prospective users assess a dataset.
Expose quality annotations or labels that help assess fitness for reuse.
Describe the purpose of data collection and the legal basis for processing personal data.

note: Sixteen scoped requirements, not an official enumerated complete gold list. Original report retained for evaluator review. Do not infer all requirements from property names.
